items.x: With a heady concept based in the cosmos, the latest record from the Dominican producer builds grand, emotional payoffs from stark arrangements inspired by vintage video games.

items.t: Skepta – The Fork and Knife
items.x: After a slightly creaky start, Skepta’s first album in seven years takes shape as a mature reflection on legacy from an icon of UK grime and a face of modern Britain.

items.t: Kings of Leon – O My Beloved
items.x: The band’s 10th album is a shocking and largely impressive reinvention that’s also the loosest they’ve sounded in decades.

items.t: Ciarán – Róisín
items.x: The former Bearface of Brockhampton emerges for a solo album of slouchy bedroom pop-soul whose cramped pileup of influences guards a promising sensitivity.

items.t: Dream Unending – Certain Uncertainties
items.x: On its third album, the dream-doom duo continues to tip the scales of its sound towards psychedelia, with a cowboy jazz record dotted with references to its creators’ metal roots.

items.t: Donald Fagen – The Nightfly
items.x: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Tonight, we join Steely Dan’s Donald Fagen under cover as an after-hours radio DJ, bringing studio perfection to the music of his adolescent dreams.

items.t: Bob Dylan – The Rolling Thunder Revue: The 1976 Live Recordings
items.x: For half a century, the spring 1976 leg of the Rolling Thunder Revue was overshadowed by the mayhem of the year before. An electrifying 39-disc box set corrects the record.
items.w: The Rolling Thunder Revue: The 1976 Live Recordings

items.t: Shygirl – Swallow!
items.x: A dreamy, guitar-heavy return from the pop experimentalist

items.t: Royal Blood – Dead Company
items.x: Brighton riff lords flex their massive muscles

items.t: untitled (halo) – untitled (halo)
items.x: The Los Angeles band’s debut puts an appealing studio gloss on the sullen, ambiguous sound of cloud rock, and the mystery doesn’t go much deeper than that.

items.t: Laila! – We’ll Never Be This Young Again
items.x: The New York songwriter and producer’s second album meditates on the passage of time, with immersive, lush songs that balance the optimism and anxiety of young adulthood.
items.w: We’ll Never Be This Young Again

items.t: nomi. – this wolf may cry
items.x: The upcoming R&B singer’s debut is a showcase for unique beats with bedroom-pop intimacy, but her restrained vocal style keeps the feelings in reserve.

items.t: gyrofield – Great Jobs
items.x: The Hong Kong-born producer moves far beyond their drum’n’bass and club-music roots, twisting dubby pulses and psychedelic sound design into shapes both introspective and exploratory.

items.t: Twisted Teens – The Holy Cross Tigers
items.x: On their third album this year, the New Orleans garage rockers embrace conflicting emotions and clashing sounds, balancing hard-charging rave-ups with exploratory tape experiments.

items.t: Yeah Yeah Yeahs – Hidden in Pieces: Live at the Royal Albert Hall
items.x: On its first live album, the New York trio recasts a quarter-century of rock songs for strings, piano, and acoustic guitar, highlighting the ache and vulnerability at the heart of its music.
items.w: Hidden in Pieces: Live at the Royal Albert Hall

items.t: Brat Star – Southern Ontario Gothic
items.x: So post-ironic it’s deadass, the Toronto songwriter’s debut renders a thoroughly modern affect with rare authenticity.

items.t: John Errol – Damage
items.x: Too challenging to qualify as radio rock, the Los Angeles songwriter’s cloudy, lo-fi grunge is stuffed with ’90s references and opaque secrets.

items.t: 1000 Rabbits return with new single ‘Stupid Boy’
items.x: Accompanying their latest release comes a surrealist and fishy video directed by Cuan Roche.

items.t: CHVRCHES drop soaring new single ‘Overthinker’
items.x: The Scottish synth-pop titans are making a mighty return with forthcoming comeback album ‘All The King’s Men’.

items.t: Daine – In Endless Awe & Agony
items.x: A modern emo gothic painted in sugary pop pastels

items.t: Chloe Qisha – Fantasize
items.x: Horny, theatrical and irresistibly catchy

items.t: Queens Of The Stone Age – Perfecth
items.x: The desert rock dons adventure into love for their third act

items.t: DIIV – ZIRP!
items.x: Pop meets politics on their most adventurous record yet

items.t: Jay Morrg – “Grab Her Nuh (Zess)”
items.x: Time for some East Coast zess as soca and dancehall meet NYC litefeet and Jersey club.

items.t: Zach Bryan – “Lies” [ft. Lana Del Rey]”
items.x: Star-crossed lovers sing right past each other on the duet from Bryan’s new Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs EP.

items.t: Olivia Rodrigo / Chappell Roan – “expectations”
items.x: If there were ever a song Chappie was born to add some sauce to, it’s “expectations.”

items.t: Zsela – “Kinda Guy”
items.x: The Los Angeles singer’s gossamer new single is a road song with an air of mystery.

items.t: G’z Up – “Fix Up (Ya Ya Ya)”
items.x: A standout cypher verse is this week’s breakout record from Dominica’s fast-moving bouyon scene.

items.t: Grimes / VADAKIN – “Accelerando”
items.x: The pop artist teases her long-awaited AI-inspired album with a new single that doesn’t quite live up to its presentation.

items.t: Star Moles – “Born Again”
items.x: Following her 2026 breakthrough, Highway to Hell, Philly songwriter Emily Moales marks her signing to Dead Oceans with a chugging, conversational new single.

items.t: Drake / Don Toliver – “Solar Eclipse”
items.x: With Texas-born crooner Don Toliver at his side, Drake reworks Ella Langley’s country hit “Choosin’ Texas” into a lounge-trap slow burn.

items.t: ki – “tissue”
items.x: Built from fragmented, pitch-shifted gurgles, the elusive artist’s latest transmission has a disarming earnestness.

items.t: Tinashe – “Popstar”
items.x: The title track of the artist’s first major label album in eight years is its lighters-up climax.

items.t: Taylor Swift – “Cleveland!”
items.x: A would-be sweet love song set in Travis Kelce’s home state is a nadir of the new The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore edition.

items.t: dBee – “syllables”
items.x: Three producers from the British rap collective step to the mic for a thunderous, brute-force blast.

items.t: Lily Konigsberg – “Free Byrd”
items.x: The Palberta and My Idea songwriter returns with a bittersweet, feel-good solo anthem.

items.t: Ella Langley – “Choosin’ Texas”
items.x: Ella Langley’s timeless, traditionalist country hit is set to become the longest-running No. 1 in U.S. history this week. Like everything else in America, it’s polarizing.

items.t: Yung Lean / Metro Boomin – “That’s It” [ft. Future]”
items.x: Three icons of 2010s hip-hop combine on the most purely Florida single from the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI soundtrack album.

items.t: Lov’nee – “Anonymat”
items.x: The Martinician rapper-singer’s new single has a little something for everyone.

items.t: kllhhr – “skin”
items.x: The ambient rapper’s surprise breakout single is a barren transmission from the other side of grief.

items.t: M(h)aol – “Scam Manifesto”
items.x: The punk band’s sardonic new single holds a mirror to social media’s insecurity influence op.

items.t: The War on Drugs – “Who’s That”
items.x: The one-off single, produced by Adam Granduciel, is a refined and revealing entry in the band’s catalog.

items.t: Fine – “Everything in the shade”
items.x: The Danish songwriter’s dreamy piano ballad is a love letter composed en plein air.

items.t: xaviersobased – “Struggle Gang”
items.x: The controlled chaos of the underground star’s newest single includes a little of everything he does best.

items.t: Dolly Parton – “I Will Always Love You”
items.x: This Saturday, we’re remembering Dolly Parton and her indelible original version of “I Will Always Love You,” a timeless declaration of loyalty and independence.

items.t: Venus Ex Machina – “Jericho”
items.x: The London musician’s forlorn and otherworldly new industrial track passes a sleepless night.

items.t: Belly Gang Kushington – “No Jewelry”
items.x: The Atlanta rapper keeps the hits coming.

items.t: Tyga – “Rack City”
items.x: On Saturdays, we go deep on one song we’ve never reviewed before. This week, we journey back to an inescapable 2011 party anthem, a canonical track that made stars out of Tyga and DJ Mustard.

items.t: Phoebe Bridgers – “I Can’t Wait”
items.x: Cameron Winter sidles up to the mic to duet with Phoebe on a standout track from her new record, Lost Weekend.

items.t: Troye Sivan – “She’s the Best”
items.x: The Australian pop singer makes his downtempo comeback with a new song and video starring Nicole Kidman.

items.t: Stella Lefty – “Boston”
items.x: Why is this cliched song that blatantly cribs Noah Kahan’s “Stick Season” everywhere right now?

items.t: Slayyyter – “Brand New Chanel$”
items.x: The sequel to “Beat Up Chanel$” is tuned to the pop radio of the early 2010s.

items.t: Kade Young – “Leswerk”
items.x: A standout from the producer’s new Gravity EP shows off the streamlined sound of contemporary Baltimore club.
